canonical_topic: Binomial model: complementary probability of a price decline
definition: In the binomial framework referenced by the author, prices are modeled as only able to rise or fall, so the probability of a decline is fully determined by the probability of a rise.
core_idea: Because the two outcomes (price rises or price falls) are exhaustive and must sum to 100%, the probability of a fall is simply one minus the probability of a rise.
key_points: The model assumes only two possible price directions: up or down.
This is stated in a footnote tied to the broader option pricing discussion, not derived from the Vega/Theta/Rho text itself.
relationships: Underlies binomial-tree style option pricing models referenced elsewhere in the chapter.

variables.P(up): probability price rises (denoted p in source)
variables.P(down): probability price falls, equals 1.0 - p in decimal form
